tutorials.title: A growth curve that draws itself
tutorials.description: A data series becomes a smooth curve that grows month by month, with a counter that follows its head and a highlighted period. One shape recipe, no chart code.
tutorials.prompt:
Draw an animated growth chart over a dark stage in my Polynite scene.

- Check commands.shape_charts, then read shapes.help.
- Put the monthly values in the shape's data and draw them with plot: an area under a line, revealed by $v0 from 0 to 1 over nine seconds.
- Mark the head of the line with a ring at #curve.b and colour the line from blue to orange with an x gradient.
- Show a counter above it with {$s[$v0*($s.n-1)]:,0} and a highlighted period box near the end.
- Add month labels, dashed grid lines and soft sounds. Record a 15-second film and check the frames.
tutorials.control_note: Changes the last value of the series in the attached example: the curve, its head and its end move. Patch c1_area and c1_count the same way so the band and the counter agree.

experiments.title: Steps instead of curves
experiments.text: Set plot.smooth to 0: the same data draws straight segments.

experiments.title: Dots only
experiments.text: Change kind to dots and add points:true to the line: a scatter chart from the same series.

experiments.title: Your own numbers
experiments.text: Replace data.s with up to 64 values; the counter, the head and the area follow without other changes.

tutorials.viewer_note: Requires commands.shape_charts (engine after 2026-10-30). Press Play: the counter and the curve share the same keys, so they stay in step in previews and recordings.

tutorials.title: Two bars, one number that keeps counting
tutorials.description: Compare two months with bars, a line between their tops and a large counter whose caption changes as the second bar keeps growing.
tutorials.prompt:
Make a bar comparison film in my scene.

- Draw a small blue bar for May and an orange bar whose height is $v0, on a dashed grid labelled 10,000 to 30,000.
- Link the tops of the two bars with a line and a ring at each end (#link.a, #link.b).
- Show RENDERS A DAY with a counter {$v0*30000:,0}: first up to 18,420 'in May', then to 25,000 'in September', ending on 25,000+.
- Use typing clicks while it counts and a confirm sound at the end. Record and verify.
tutorials.control_note: Sets the orange bar outside the film's keys (a preview). Inside a film the keys drive v0.

experiments.title: Three months
experiments.text: Use plot kind:'bars' with data [1860, 9100, 18420]: the same frame with a series instead of hand-placed boxes.

tutorials.viewer_note: Requires commands.shape_charts. Counters format with thousands separators through {expr:,0}.

tutorials.title: An agent, its tools and a file read dot by dot
tutorials.description: Curved links carry pulses from an agent to four tools, a file is scanned byte by byte, and its dots fly into four named clusters. Every dot is one copy of a repeated item with its own $i.
tutorials.prompt:
Explain how an AI agent reverse-engineers a file, as a motion graphic.

- Draw an AI box, four tool boxes with small icons drawn from dots and boxes, and cubic links between them.
- Send two pulses along each link with #l0.along(fract($t*0.42+$i/2)).
- Draw the file as a 14 x 9 grid of dots (one repeated circle, positions from $i with mod and floor). Light each dot as a cursor box passes it and grow a progress bar.
- Then move dots from the file into four clusters with hash and smooth, label them with addresses, and rename them to functions.
- Keep each shape under 512 strokes; split clusters into two shapes if tiles run out. Record and verify the end frame.
tutorials.control_note: Makes the pulses on the first link larger. Discover item indexes with shapes.status before patching another scene.

experiments.title: Faster scan
experiments.text: Divide the 5 in the scan's rate by two: the cursor and the lit dots stay in step.

experiments.title: More pulses
experiments.text: Set the pulse repeat to 4 and use $i/4 in along(): evenly spaced packets.

tutorials.viewer_note: Requires commands.shape_charts. Scattered moving dots need many tiles: the engine refuses a shape over 192 tiles with a clear message; split it.

tutorials.title: A waveform with words that light up
tutorials.description: A voice envelope drawn as mirrored bars, lit up to a moving playhead, a cut marker, and each word highlighted with its own note when the playhead reaches it.
tutorials.prompt:
Show a short spoken line as an edited waveform.

- Put 60 envelope values in data and draw them twice with plot kind:'bars' (one with a negative height for the mirror).
- Draw the same bars in white with reveal:$v0 and a playhead line at x = X0 + $v0*W with its time {$v0*8:1} s.
- Add a CUT marker. Write the words in grey and, for each word, a white copy shown by the film while the playhead crosses it, with a short synthesized note.
- Record and check the sound.
tutorials.control_note: Makes the playhead faster in the attached example; move the word cues by the same factor to keep them in time.

experiments.title: Another voice
experiments.text: Replace data.e with your own envelope (0..1, up to 64 values).

experiments.title: A line instead of bars
experiments.text: Use kind:'area' with smooth:1 for a softer waveform.

tutorials.viewer_note: Requires commands.shape_charts. Word notes use shape sfx.notes: no audio file is needed.
